pull.title: fix: custom providers 500'd, fallback chains could never fire, 5.6 models hidden
pull.body:
Four defects, each reproduced before it was fixed. Diagnosis came from the live 1.7 GB request log, not from reading code.

## 1. Adding a custom provider returned HTTP 500, always

`admin_custom_routes` was written against an imagined registry contract while the real `ProviderRegistry` landed in a parallel worktree. They drifted:

```
$ curl -X POST /admin/api/custom-providers -d '{"display_name":"My Test Gateway",...}'
{"error":{"message":"ProviderRegistry.add() missing 2 required positional
 arguments: 'base_url' and 'api_keys'"}}
HTTP 500
```

The tests were green because they injected a fake registry shaped like the guess. **That fake is why this shipped.** It is gone — the suite now drives the real `ProviderRegistry` against `tmp_path`, so the contract cannot drift again. The module's duck-typed mirror, its `importlib` indirection and its second copy of the slug rule are deleted; `custom_provider_id()` on the registry is the one implementation.

## 2. No request has *ever* been served by a fallback

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM requests WHERE route_attempt > 0;   -- 0
```

Routing was never at fault — the sonnet route resolves to three attempts correctly. Two things upstream made the chain unreachable.

**The holdback window never protected anything.** `RecoveryHoldbackBuffer` retains the first 0.75 s of SSE so an early cutoff can be retried invisibly. Its clock started on the locally-built `message_start` frame, pushed *before* the upstream request goes out. Measured time-to-first-token on this traffic is 9–184 s, so the window was always already expired and every stream committed on its first upstream byte. It now starts when the upstream stream opens.

**Non-streaming requests committed on the first chunk** although the client sees nothing until the end — the handler aggregates the whole SSE into one JSON message. Nothing is on the wire, so nothing is committed. Those chunks are now held and dropped with the failed attempt, and the chain continues. 24 of the 62 mid-stream failures in the log were non-streaming and could all have been rescued.

Unchanged and deliberate: a streaming client past its first chunk does not fall back, because swapping models mid-answer would splice two completions.

## 3. An exhausted chain reported as a primary failure

`on_attempt` only fired for the attempt that streamed, so a request that walked three models and failed logged `route_attempt=0`. It now fires before each attempt, which is what makes the Served-by-fallback card and the Failover panel honest.

## 4. Images went to models known to be blind

The vision policy only diverted when `MODEL_VISION` was set. With it unset, an image went to a primary whose own metadata says it rejects images, then to the next blind model in the chain. A chain member known to accept images now leads instead, and known-blind entries are dropped from an image request either way. When nothing is known to see, the route is left intact rather than emptied.

## 5. ChatGPT OAuth exposed 4 models and hid the whole 5.6 family

The backend's models endpoint answers 401 for an OAuth session, so the catalog cannot come from the gateway (probed; the endpoint is not usable this way). It now comes from the models.dev `openai` catalog FCC already fetches and caches, filtered by the same allowlist rule, falling back to the static ids when the cache is absent. An explicit `gpt-5.6` exclusion contradicted the provider's own `>5.4` heuristic and is removed.

```
before: gpt-5.3-codex-spark, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.5
after:  + gpt-5.6, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra
```

## Verification

**A real fallback, end to end, real provider and credentials.** Primary set to `nvidia_nim/deliberately/not-a-real-model`, chain to `opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free`:

```
HTTP 200   "model": "deepseek-v4-flash-free"

{'requested_model': 'claude-sonnet-4-6', 'provider': 'opencode',
 'resolved_model': 'deepseek-v4-flash-free', 'status': 'success',
 'route_attempt': 1,
 'route_primary_model': 'nvidia_nim/deliberately/not-a-real-model'}

/admin/api/requests/stats ->
  served_by_fallback = 1
  fallback_routes = [{"primary": "nvidia_nim/deliberately/not-a-real-model",
                      "served_by": "opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free", "count": 1}]
```

This is the first time a request has gone through a fallback chain in this project.

**Custom provider create against a real server** on a throwaway home: HTTP 200, persisted to `custom_providers.json`, listed, key masked in every response, duplicate name 409.

**Nous `/models`** confirms `tencent/hy3:free` publishes `input_modalities: ["text"]`, so the vision diversion is live for this configuration.

**Suite:** 3337 passed, 6 failed — the documented PowerShell installer baseline, identical on unmodified `main`. `ruff format`, `ruff check` and `ty` clean.

## Residual risks

- A streaming client still cannot fall back once its first chunk is out. Recovering that means putting the chain inside the provider's midstream recovery, which is an architecture change rather than a fix.
- No live image request was made: the stored ChatGPT OAuth token is expired, so the vision diversion is proven by provider metadata and unit tests, not a round trip.
- Non-streaming requests now report `ttft_ms` close to `duration_ms`, since the client genuinely receives nothing earlier. 144 of the last 20 000 requests were non-streaming.
- models.dev is a third-party catalog. If it lists an `openai` model the OAuth backend does not serve, that model appears in the picker and fails on use. The static fallback list bounds the damage when the cache is missing, not when it is wrong.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commit.message:
fix: custom providers 500'd, fallback chains could never fire, 5.6 models hidden

Four defects found by reading the live 1.7 GB request log and reproducing each
against a real server, not by reading code.

**Adding a custom provider returned HTTP 500, always.**
`admin_custom_routes` was written against an imagined registry contract while
the real `ProviderRegistry` landed in a parallel worktree, and the two drifted:
`add()` takes the fields and allocates the id, not a prebuilt entry.

    ProviderRegistry.add() missing 2 required positional arguments:
    'base_url' and 'api_keys'

The tests stayed green because they injected a fake shaped like the guess. The
fake is gone; the suite now drives the real registry at `tmp_path`, so the
contract cannot drift again. The module's duck-typed mirror, dynamic importlib
lookup and second copy of the slug rule are deleted -- `custom_provider_id()`
on the registry is now the one implementation.

**No request in 1.7 GB of log has ever been served by a fallback.**
`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM requests WHERE route_attempt > 0` returns 0. Routing was
never the problem: the sonnet route resolves to three attempts correctly. Two
things upstream of it made the chain unreachable.

1. The holdback window never protected anything. `RecoveryHoldbackBuffer`
   exists to retain the first 0.75s of SSE so an early cutoff can be retried
   invisibly, but its clock started on the locally-built `message_start` frame,
   pushed *before* the upstream request goes out. Measured time-to-first-token
   on this traffic is 9-184s, so the window was always already expired and
   every stream committed on its first upstream byte. The window now starts
   when the upstream stream opens.

2. Non-streaming requests committed on the provider's first chunk even though
   the client sees nothing until the end -- the handler aggregates the whole
   SSE into one JSON message. Nothing is on the wire, so nothing is committed:
   those attempts are now held and dropped with the attempt that failed, and
   the chain continues. 24 of the 62 mid-stream failures in the log were
   non-streaming and could all have been rescued.

For a streaming client past its first chunk the rule is unchanged and
deliberate: swapping models mid-answer would splice two completions.

**An exhausted chain reported as a primary failure.** `on_attempt` only fired
for the attempt that streamed, so a request that walked three models and failed
logged `route_attempt=0`. It now fires before each attempt is tried, which is
what makes the Served-by-fallback card and Failover panel honest.

**An image went to models known to be blind.** The vision policy only diverted
when `MODEL_VISION` was set; with it unset the image was sent to a primary
whose own metadata says it rejects images, then to the next blind model in the
chain. A chain member known to accept images now leads instead, and known-blind
entries are dropped from an image request either way. When nothing is known to
see, the route is left intact rather than emptied.

**ChatGPT OAuth exposed 4 models and hid the whole 5.6 family.** The backend's
models endpoint answers 401 for an OAuth session, so the catalog cannot come
from the gateway. It now comes from the models.dev `openai` catalog that FCC
already fetches and caches, filtered by the same allowlist rule, falling back
to the static ids when the cache is absent. An explicit `gpt-5.6` exclusion
contradicted the provider's own ">5.4" heuristic and is removed. 4 -> 8 models,
including `gpt-5.6-luna`, which people were already configuring by hand.

Verification:
- Custom provider create against a real server on a throwaway home: HTTP 200,
  persisted to `custom_providers.json`, listed, key masked in every response,
  duplicate name 409.
- A real fallback end to end, real provider, real credentials: primary set to
  `nvidia_nim/deliberately/not-a-real-model`, chain to
  `opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free`. HTTP 200, answered by the fallback, and
  the row reads `route_attempt=1`,
  `route_primary_model=nvidia_nim/deliberately/not-a-real-model`. The stats
  endpoint reports `served_by_fallback=1` with the primary -> served_by path.
- Nous `/models` confirms `tencent/hy3:free` publishes `input_modalities:
  ["text"]`, so the vision diversion is live for this configuration.
- Full suite: 3337 passed, 6 failed -- the documented PowerShell installer
  baseline, identical on unmodified main. ruff format, ruff check and ty clean.

Not done: a streaming client still cannot fall back once its first chunk is
out. Recovering that needs the chain inside the provider's midstream recovery,
which is an architecture change, not a fix. No live image request was made --
the stored ChatGPT OAuth token is expired, so vision diversion is proven by
metadata and unit tests, not a round trip.
